messages.message: `pages/ArchitecturePage/` contains `ArchitectureMap/index.tsx` — a screen folder holds its two halves ONLY (`component.tsx` = the shape, `index.tsx` = the wiring). Whatever this is, it has a real home: a component of its own goes to `blocks/<category>/`, a fetch goes to `hooks/`, a pure helper to `modules/utils/`, a shape to `modules/types/`, copy or a config map to `resources/`. "Only this screen uses it" is how a folder becomes a second codebase.
Import '@heroui/react' outside the vocabulary tier — use the matching atom (vendor wrapped once); if missing, add an atom instead of importing vendor directly.

JSX file without an `identity` prop on the root — add `identity={{ tier: "…", component: "…" }}` on the root frame/composite (see components/frames/_identity.ts); do not wrap with a hand-rolled data-tier div.
`WithClassNames<…>` at sentence tier opens a className backdoor (BLOCK-4) — push the difference down one tier and name it.
`cn(...)` outside the vocabulary tier (BLOCK-5) — treat this as a missing composite or missing variant; do not assemble classes here.
`flex` on <div> at sentence tier — this tier composes frames/composites and does not draw layout; push the class down into a frame/composite.

messages.message: `pages/ProfileOverviewPage/` contains `ProfileJobReadiness/index.tsx` — a screen folder holds its two halves ONLY (`component.tsx` = the shape, `index.tsx` = the wiring). Whatever this is, it has a real home: a component of its own goes to `blocks/<category>/`, a fetch goes to `hooks/`, a pure helper to `modules/utils/`, a shape to `modules/types/`, copy or a config map to `resources/`. "Only this screen uses it" is how a folder becomes a second codebase.
